question: The distance between a man and a 230m long train is 115 m. How much time (in seconds) will the train, which is running at a speed of 60 km/h, take to pass the man who is running at a speed of 9 km/h towards the train?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of train = 60 km/h

Speed of man = 9 km/h

Train length = 230 m

Distance between Man and Train = 115 m

**Concept used:**

Relative Speed = Relative Distance/Time

Where Relative speed is sum of man and train speed because they move towards each other.

**Calculation:**

Relative Distance = 230 + 115

⇒ 345 m 

Relative speed = Speed of train + speed of man

⇒ 60 + 9 = 69 km/h

⇒ 69 × (5/18) m/sec

Time taken to pass the man = Relative Distance/Relative speed

⇒ frac {345}{(69 times 5/18)}

⇒ 18 sec

**∴ The Required time is 18 sec.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**If the man and the train move towards each other then 

Relative speed = Speed of train + Speed of man.

If the man and the train move in same direction then,

Relative Speed = Speed of train - Speed of man.
